RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the successful candidate are men, so the all-male composition of the panel provides no basis for a claim of sex discrimination. Raising gender would undermine your professional credibility, as sex was not a distinguishing factor between the candidates.

The decision likely came down to how the panel prioritized qualifications for a department-head role: your specialized doctoral background and section experience versus the other candidate's formal management training and broader leadership profile.

Instead of focusing on panel demographics, send a polite follow-up requesting your feedback. Frame the inquiry around professional development, asking specifically how you can strengthen your leadership credentials for future executive appointments.
